egress.terms: The page headline states the rates: 'Rotating Residentialfrom $1.50/GB ISP Proxiesfrom $2.00/IP Rotating Mobilefrom $2.00/GB'. GB plans 'roll over and never expires'. Static ISP is 'Priced per dedicated IP, monthly. Unlimited traffic, with a fair use cap of 100 GB per IP per month, so there is no bandwidth to buy.' Dedicated mobile advertises 'UNLIMITED GB'.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 1.50/GB residential, i.e. USD 1,536 per TiB; USD 2.00/IP/month for static ISP; mobile metered at $2/GB or unlimited on a dedicated port

record.interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 with country, region, city, ZIP, ISP, ASN and OS targeting on the rotating products; a fixed address on the static residential and dedicated mobile products.
record.chaining: The cheapest credible metered residential rate found ($1.50/GB) and, separately, a $2/month static ISP address and a dedicated mobile port with unlimited bandwidth: one vendor showing all three price shapes side by side, which is why the 'residential egress' question cannot be answered with a single $/GB number.

limits.value: rotating products are metered and unused GB rolls over and never expires; static ISP is sold per address with a 100 GB per IP per month fair-use cap; dedicated mobile is sold per device with unlimited GB

record.limits_note: Unused GB rolling over changes the arithmetic for a bursty workload but not for a steady 1 TiB month, which spends the allowance every month by construction.
record.binding_note: For the metered product the allowance is the binding constraint at USD 1,536 a TiB; for the $2 static ISP address nothing in the vocabulary binds and the terms of the debrid service become the limit.

identity_cost.detail: Self-service account with card; the trial costs $1.97 rather than requiring a free registration.

record.confidence_note: The three headline rates are in the page title and the body, read. The per-product detail pages were not opened, so the exact terms behind 'unlimited bandwidth' on the mobile port are untested.
